Annual and interim statements print different lines: the annual income statement states acquisition-related costs, interest expense and interest income separately, the interim statements state interest expense, net, and several cash flow lines exist in only one of the two; the cells that cannot be filled are marked as not supplied, severity Low, closed by restating the interim statements on the annual layout.

Cells that the source prints as a dash, such as the goodwill impairment charge in the 2026 periods, are marked as not supplied and never read as zero; severity Low, closed by the issuer confirming nil.

The first and second quarter 2026 income statements and cash flows are not carried as columns; the third quarter and nine month columns are, and the earlier quarters are only in the balance sheet; severity Low, closed by adding those columns from the first and second quarter reports.

Share repurchases after September 30, 2026 are visible only as a lower share count on the cover of the third-quarter report and have no stated amount, so no post-balance-sheet adjustment is made; severity Low, closed by the repurchase amounts in the next report.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings are concentrated in a business tied to combustion and hybrid vehicle output. Performance Materials supplied 52.0% of FY2025 net sales and 77.9% of segment EBITDA at a 53.8% margin, against margins of 15.1% in Performance Chemicals and 20.0% in Advanced Polymer Technologies, so a fall in vehicle production, a weaker emissions standard or the loss of one of about 65 automotive customers moves group cash flow far more than any other segment could. facts.text: The credit strengths, in rank order, are these. First, pricing power and margin in Performance Materials: a 55.6% nine-month margin and USD 14.3 million of price and mix against a USD 1.3 million volume loss mean earnings held while volume stalled, which supports debt service. Second, moderate leverage and cover: net debt is 2.75x LTM Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 6.66x, which leaves room to absorb a modest earnings decline. Third, adequate liquidity of USD 398.2 million with a revolver to 2031-03-31, which covers near-term maturities not funded by the trust 5.21x. Fourth, a record of debt reduction, USD 255.5 million since FY2024, which lowers the amount to refinance. Fifth, flexible capital expenditure and detailed, audited reporting, which allow cash preservation and lender monitoring. facts.label: PEST factors
facts.text: Regulatory and political factors are material. Emission standards set carbon demand and the annual report names the risk that standards are not tightened, retaliatory tariffs by China could lower margin on carbon and chemicals exported from the United States, and pavement demand follows government infrastructure budgets. Economic factors are also material: crude-oil-driven asphalt costs limited pavement growth, 43% of FY2025 sales were outside the United States with exposure to the euro, yen, pound, real and renminbi, and a hypothetical 10 percent adverse move in three currencies would cut nine-month net sales by USD 11.1 million. Technological change is the most important: electric and hydrogen vehicles and sealed tanks threaten automotive carbon demand over time, and social factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Ingevity presents an adequate business profile supported by a high-margin automotive carbon franchise with pricing power, moderate leverage of 2.75x and liquidity of USD 398.2 million, but credit quality is constrained by earnings concentration, shareholder returns above free cash flow and an unfinished portfolio reshaping. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because price and mix, a flexible capital expenditure budget and a shrinking debt balance offset volume softness, although free cash flow swung between 14% and 73% of Adjusted EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on whether an Advanced Polymer Technologies sale repays debt, on the pace of repurchases, and on handling the USD 550.0 million 2028 notes before the revolver test on 2028-08-02. Primary downside path: weaker automotive volume in Asia and Europe lowering Performance Materials EBITDA, which carries 88.2% of Adjusted EBITDA, while repurchases and an unfinished sale leave leverage higher into the 2028 refinancing. Further analysis would require the financing agreements, the proxy statement, the use of disposal proceeds, a rating or bond price and any sale agreement for Advanced Polymer Technologies. Top risk: concentration of earnings in automotive carbon combined with the 2028 refinancing. spans.text: # Source readiness: Ingevity Corp (ngvt-1653477)
## Request

Source readiness for Ingevity Corp (issuer ngvt-1653477) as of 2026-11-18, for the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the five supplied SEC filings, two annual reports and three quarterly reports, checked against the evidence that Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit need.
## Sources

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-11-05 (signature date; filing date not stated) | 24cb83622602b7b764fe489a9591b0d3e14c2ce21daf156ba011444eb0c69811 | Latest balance sheet and nine-month 2026 statements, debt, covenants, liquidity, divestitures, segment results, outlook |
No earlier module output was supplied to this module; it is the entry point of the run.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The five Ingevity filings are sufficient for a credit snapshot, but guarantor, security, covenant-definition and board facts rest on filing summaries because the financing agreements, proxy statement and any rating are not supplied. Creditors should treat those four areas as unverified until the documents arrive.

The latest filing was signed 13 days before the as-of date, so the balance sheet at September 30, 2026 is the freshest evidence and nothing dated after November 5, 2026 was supplied. FY2024 figures must be taken from the 2025 annual report, which recasts them for the industrial specialties disposal.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; calculation C7
### Key findings

The reporting entity is single and clear: Ingevity Corporation, a Delaware company listed in New York, files consolidated statements with no parent company named and no separate restricted-group figures. The revolving credit agreement also names Ingevity Holdings SRL and Ingevity UK Ltd as parties, so the borrowers extend beyond the listed parent, but no filing names the subsidiary guarantors of the 2028 senior notes.

Period coverage is sufficient for the run's current and prior periods. The three 2026 quarterly reports give consecutive quarter-end balance sheets with year-to-date results, and the audited 2025 annual report gives FY2025 with FY2024 and FY2023 recast, so Q3 2026 and FY2025 can be built from the filings alone. The September 30, 2025 balance sheet is not in any supplied document, so prior-year interim comparisons are limited to income statement, cash flow and equity items.

Comparability needs care because the reporting perimeter changed twice. The industrial specialties business, sold on January 1, 2026, is reported as discontinued operations, while the road markings product line stayed in continuing results until its sale on April 15, 2026, so FY2025 and the first months of 2026 include road markings revenue that the company no longer has. FY2024 net sales are USD 1,406.4 million in the 2024 annual report and USD 1,200.1 million recast in the 2025 annual report, and the USD 206.3 million difference equals the discontinued business's FY2024 net sales.

Debt and liquidity evidence is complete enough for Financial foundation and Liquidity work. The debt note lists every instrument and ties to the balance sheet after issuance costs, and the stated revolver availability ties to commitments, drawings and letters of credit. At September 30, 2026 debt including finance leases was USD 1,147.8 million, undrawn revolver capacity was USD 312.8 million and cash was USD 85.4 million, of which USD 81.1 million was held by foreign subsidiaries.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

Claims outside the debt table are documented: leases, retirement plans and the BASF litigation, which was accrued at USD 95.4 million within accrued expenses at December 31, 2025 and settled by cash payments of USD 113.2 million on April 1, 2026. The filings disclose no supplier finance or factoring, and the receivables securitization is reported inside debt.

Covenant compliance is reported but cannot be recomputed from the filings. At September 30, 2026 the issuer states net leverage of 2.4x against a 4.0x maximum and interest coverage of 7.0x against a 3.0x minimum, on credit agreement definitions that are not in the sources, so any leverage computed from the statements will differ from the covenant figure in a way that cannot be reconciled.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

The company's earnings measure ties across documents. The three 2026 quarterly figures of Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations sum to the nine-month USD 314.5 million, and the segment note reaches the same total after corporate costs, so the 2026 series is internally consistent.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_ngvt-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ngvt-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation C4; calculation C6

Business & governance can describe strategy, transactions and management, but not board structure, ownership or pay, because the annual report incorporates those items from a proxy statement that was not supplied. Finance leadership also changed: the 2025 annual report names Mary Dean Hall as Chief Financial Officer, while the three 2026 quarterly reports are signed by Phillip J. Platt as Chief Financial Officer, and no supplied filing states why beyond a general forward-looking reference to leadership transitions.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The main evidence against calling the sources ready is the unfinished sale process for the Advanced Polymer Technologies segment, which contributed USD 30.5 million of nine-month 2026 segment EBITDA. A sale agreement signed after November 5, 2026 would change the reporting perimeter and every pro forma figure, and none of the supplied documents could show it. The view would move to conditional for Financial foundation if any filing or announcement dated between November 5 and November 18, 2026 reports such an agreement.

A second counterargument is that the missing documents are public and already summarised in the filings, so their absence may change little. The indenture and credit agreement are listed as exhibits and covenant compliance is reported with the issuer's own ratios. That argument would win if the agreements confirm the guarantor group, security and definitions the filings summarise, which would close both material gaps and let Fundamental credit state structure with source support.
### Limitations

No executed financing document is supplied, so guarantor identity, the security position of the revolving credit facility, restricted-group composition and covenant definitions come from filing summaries.
No credit rating, market price, peer set or portfolio information is supplied, and none of the filings states a rating for the issuer.

Cash flow statements include discontinued operations and cover year-to-date periods, so discrete-quarter and continuing-operations cash flows are not stated and need differencing or remain not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5
The quarterly reports state signature dates rather than filing dates, so the publication dates used here are signature dates.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59

Financial foundation for Ingevity Corp (issuer ngvt-1653477) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: consolidated FY2024 and FY2025, the nine months and third quarter of 2026 against 2025, carrying-value debt, liquidity, reported and issuer-adjusted earnings and cash interest cover, with the debt maturity ladder at 2026-09-30.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Ingevity has cut debt including finance leases to USD 1,145.5 million, with net debt at 2.75x the issuer's adjusted EBITDA but 5.35x unadjusted EBITDA, so creditor comfort depends on whether the add-backs recur.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C06; calculation C08

Debt including finance leases is USD 255.5 million lower than at December 2024, but free cash flow in the nine months of 2026 was only USD 49.1 million after a USD 113.2 million litigation payment, while disposal proceeds of USD 156.3 million exceeded share repurchases of USD 125.3 million, so the reduction leans on sales that will not recur. The gap between the two EBITDA measures is impairment, restructuring and litigation charges that the issuer excludes.

### Financial interpretation

Net debt fell from USD 1,333.0 million at December 2024 to USD 1,060.1 million at September 2026, and net debt over adjusted EBITDA eased from 3.54x to 2.75x. On unadjusted EBITDA the last twelve months ratio is 5.35x, because impairment, restructuring and litigation charges sit inside it, and FY2025 unadjusted EBITDA of only USD 36.2 million means the annual unadjusted ratios say little about debt capacity.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; calculation C02; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C08

In the nine months of 2026 operating cash flow was USD 83.4 million after the USD 113.2 million litigation settlement payment and capital expenditures were USD 34.3 million, leaving free cash flow of USD 49.1 million, while sales of businesses brought in USD 156.3 million and share repurchases took USD 125.3 million. Debt including finance leases is USD 63.0 million lower than at December 2025, so the improvement depends on proceeds that will not recur and on a smaller earnings base, since the last twelve months of adjusted EBITDA still include the road markings line until its sale on April 15, 2026 and the filings do not state its earnings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32–34; calculation C01; calculation C12; calculation C13

Cash interest cover on adjusted EBITDA rose from 4.41x in FY2024 to 6.66x over the last twelve months as cash interest paid fell from USD 85.4 million to USD 57.8 million alongside lower debt. Cover on unadjusted EBITDA is 3.43x for the last twelve months and below one time in both annual periods, so coverage depends on the issuer-adjusted measure. The cash figure includes discontinued operations, whose interest expense is nil.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C07; calculation C08

Cash conversion is uneven. Free cash flow was USD 273.5 million in FY2025 against USD 51.0 million in FY2024, and USD 49.1 million in the nine months of 2026 against adjusted EBITDA of USD 314.5 million, held down by the litigation payment. Working capital absorbed cash in the nine months of 2026: the cash flow statement shows USD 38.8 million spent on receivables and USD 15.9 million on inventories. Capital expenditures stayed near USD 34.3 million for the nine months, both years, so they are not what moves free cash flow.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; calculation C13

Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was USD 398.2 million, made up of USD 85.4 million of cash and USD 312.8 million of undrawn revolver availability, against USD 156.4 million of debt maturing within one year. That current debt is the USD 75.0 million receivables securitization, the USD 80.0 million finance lease due in January 2027 and USD 1.4 million of smaller lease principal; a USD 86.6 million restricted investment is held to settle the lease and is not counted in cash. The revolver commitments were cut from USD 1 billion to USD 750 million on March 26, 2026 and now mature in 2031, but would mature 91 days before the 2028 notes if more than USD 250 million of them remain, so the USD 550.0 million notes and the USD 425.0 million of revolver drawings share one refinancing date in 2028.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C03; calculation C11

Three definition risks limit comparisons. The cash flow statements do not segregate discontinued operations while the income statement does, FY2024 sales are USD 1,406.4 million as first reported and USD 1,200.1 million recast, and the covenant leverage of 2.4x is on credit agreement definitions that differ from the method figure of 2.75x in a way that cannot be reconciled from the filings. There is no contract liability, deposit or supplier finance funding float: the third-quarter report states no contract liabilities existed in any period shown.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2024-12-31_ngvt-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; calculation C08

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The main evidence that leverage is better than the unadjusted ratios suggest is that the issuer reports covenant net leverage of 2.4x against a 4.0x maximum and interest coverage of 7.0x against a 3.0x minimum, and that net debt over adjusted EBITDA is 2.75x. That view would win if the credit agreement allows the add-backs the issuer takes, which cannot be checked without the agreement.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; calculation C08

The main evidence against comfort is that adjusted EBITDA of USD 373.0 million for FY2025 includes add-backs of USD 336.8 million, of which impairments are USD 293.1 million, and that the nine months of 2026 add back a further litigation charge of USD 16.2 million and portfolio review costs. A sale of the Advanced Polymer Technologies segment, which earned USD 30.5 million of nine-month segment EBITDA, would shrink the base again, so net debt over adjusted EBITDA would be worse unless proceeds repay debt.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; calculation C06; calculation C14
### Limitations

Unadjusted EBITDA is derived here from statement lines because the company reports none, so it is a calculation and not an issuer figure; a different definition of the add-backs would move both ratios on it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation C04
Twelve-month ratios are built only for the period to September 30, 2026; the earlier 2026 quarter ends carry balance sheet and liquidity figures but no leverage or cover ratio.

No debt maturity table is printed in the filings, so the ladder uses the balance sheet split of debt maturing within one year and the stated maturity dates, and the timing of the securitization and of the smaller finance leases is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; calculation C03
Cash interest and capital expenditures cannot be restated to continuing operations, so ratios built on them carry the discontinued business as printed.

## Gaps

Unadjusted EBITDA is not stated by the company, so it was derived from net income, interest, tax and depreciation and amortization for every period; it restricts the leverage and cover charts to a calculated measure, severity Medium, and would be closed by the issuer stating one or by an agreed definition.

The cash flow statements include discontinued operations and are not segregated, so cash interest, capital expenditures and operating cash flow cannot be restated to continuing operations; severity Medium, closed by the discontinued operations cash flow detail, which the annual report gives only for selected items.

No debt maturity schedule is printed, and the maturity of the receivables securitization and the timing of the smaller finance leases are not stated; the ladder therefore uses the balance sheet classification and is severity Medium, closed by the notes or the facility agreements.

Instrument carrying values are not disclosed, so the instrument table carries principal and one aggregate financing cost adjustment; severity Low, closed by the allocation of issuance costs by instrument.

The security, guarantee and legal rank of the revolving credit facility, the receivables securitization and the finance leases are not stated, and the guarantors of the 2028 notes are not named, so the debt stack is not drawn and cumulative leverage is not stated; severity High, closed by the credit agreement, the indenture and the securitization agreement.

Covenant net leverage and interest coverage are stated only on credit agreement definitions, so headroom against the 4.0x and 3.0x tests is not calculable; severity High, closed by the credit agreement and the covenant compliance certificate definitions.

The road markings line sold on April 15, 2026 stays in continuing results and in the last twelve months, and its sales and earnings are not separately stated for the periods to its sale except for net sales of USD 12.9 million in the nine months of 2026; severity Medium, closed by segment detail or pro forma figures from the issuer.

Leverage and cover ratios are built for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026 only; the quarter ends of March and June 2026 have balance sheet figures but no twelve-month ratio, severity Low, closed by constructing them from the first and second quarter reports.
The balance sheet at September 30, 2025 is not in any supplied document, so debt and cash are not compared at that date; severity Low, closed by the third-quarter 2025 report.

Annual and interim statements print different lines: the annual income statement states acquisition-related costs, interest expense and interest income separately, the interim statements state interest expense, net, and several cash flow lines exist in only one of the two; the cells that cannot be filled are marked as not supplied, severity Low, closed by restating the interim statements on the annual layout.

Cells that the source prints as a dash, such as the goodwill impairment charge in the 2026 periods, are marked as not supplied and never read as zero; severity Low, closed by the issuer confirming nil.

The first and second quarter 2026 income statements and cash flows are not carried as columns; the third quarter and nine month columns are, and the earlier quarters are only in the balance sheet; severity Low, closed by adding those columns from the first and second quarter reports.

Share repurchases after September 30, 2026 are visible only as a lower share count on the cover of the third-quarter report and have no stated amount, so no post-balance-sheet adjustment is made; severity Low, closed by the repurchase amounts in the next report.

No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Ingevity is a widely held listed company with no controlling owner or sponsor named in the filings, so creditors rely on management's own financial policy, which in 2026 cut debt but returned more cash to shareholders than free cash flow covered. Debt including finance leases fell USD 63.0 million to USD 1,145.5 million in the nine months to September 30, 2026, while share repurchases of USD 125.3 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 49.1 million after the USD 113.2 million BASF settlement, and the company does not say whether sale proceeds of USD 156.3 million paid for them.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation A6; calculation A8

Earnings rest on one business: Performance Materials, which sells activated carbon for vehicle fuel-vapor systems, produced 77.9% of FY2025 segment EBITDA. Two disposals completed in 2026 and a third segment for sale mean the company creditors lend to is still changing shape.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 145; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation A3
### Key findings

The filings give no owner or sponsor behaviour to assess and no owner support to count on. They name no controlling shareholder, just over four thousand holders of record held the shares in February 2026, and the only outside investor named, Vision One Fund, signed a cooperation agreement on 2025-03-30 that settled a board contest and carried a standstill until the nomination window for the 2026 annual meeting opened. Its stake is not stated, and who holds the largest positions is not established because the 2025 annual report takes ownership and board information from a proxy statement that is not supplied, so a creditor cannot judge whether an equity cure or a holder-driven shareholder return is likely.

Earnings are concentrated in a business tied to combustion and hybrid vehicle output. Performance Materials supplied 52.0% of FY2025 net sales and 77.9% of segment EBITDA at a 53.8% margin, against margins of 15.1% in Performance Chemicals and 20.0% in Advanced Polymer Technologies, so a fall in vehicle production, a weaker emissions standard or the loss of one of about 65 automotive customers moves group cash flow far more than any other segment could. The annual report puts the ten largest customers at about 90% of sales in this business, around half of its sales are in North America and about 40% in Asia Pacific, and sealed fuel tanks and electric vehicles are named as substitutes.

Portfolio change has been fast and is not finished. ### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious reading of financial policy is that borrowing fell and covenant headroom is stated as wide: the issuer reports net leverage of 2.4x against a 4.0x maximum and interest coverage of 7.0x against a 3.0x minimum, revolver borrowings fell USD 92.0 million, and the road markings assets were written down before their sale closed. Management also describes North American automotive demand as resilient on hybrid vehicle preference, and Performance Materials held a nine-month margin of 55.6%. The cautious reading would lose if proceeds of an Advanced Polymer Technologies sale repay debt, the unused USD 172.2 million of repurchase authorization is largely left unused, and the 2028 notes are refinanced before the revolver maturity springs forward.

The strongest evidence against treating Performance Materials concentration as a weakness is its stability: net sales of USD 606.9 million in FY2025 were close to USD 609.6 million in FY2024, and nine-month sales rose to USD 470.1 million from USD 455.7 million on pricing, with the margin up to 55.6% from 54.5%. The concentration view would strengthen if volumes keep falling, as they did by USD 6.7 million, or four percent, in the third quarter on softness in China and Europe, and it would soften if hybrid vehicle share keeps offsetting lower combustion output. A named controlling holder, or a proxy statement showing large holders with creditor-aligned positions, would change the ownership view.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No new notes or term debt were issued in 2025 or in 2026 to September 30 in the filings supplied; the senior unsecured notes due 2028, USD 550.0 million issued on 2020-10-28, remain the only bond. The one financing transaction in the period is the second amendment and restatement of the revolving credit facility on 2026-03-26, which cut commitments from USD 1,000 million to USD 750 million, moved maturity to 2031-03-31 and cost fees of USD 4.0 million. The new maturity advances to 91 days before the 2028 notes mature if more than USD 250 million of them remain outstanding, and the margin on benchmark-rate loans is 1.00% to 1.75%. Receivables securitization borrowings rose from USD 43.9 million to USD 75.0 million within a facility of up to USD 100.0 million.

The industrial specialties product line and the North Charleston crude tall oil refinery were sold to Mainstream Pine Products, LLC under an agreement signed on 2025-09-03 and completed on 2026-01-01 for cash proceeds of USD 93.1 million, with a gain of USD 54.0 million in discontinued operations. The sale came with a transition services agreement of up to 12 months, a four-year limited non-compete, a ground lease and a reciprocal plant operating agreement of 20 years each with renewals, an intellectual property agreement and an environmental indemnity, which keep the two companies operating side by side on the North Charleston site. In the nine months to September 30, 2026 the company also sold its DeRidder, Louisiana facility, extinguishing a USD 7.8 million retirement obligation and recording an USD 8.2 million guarantee of the purchaser's environmental obligations through 2027-06-30.

The road markings product line was sold to PPG Industries Inc. on 2026-04-15. The first-quarter report gave a price of USD 65 million subject to adjustments and the later reports give cash proceeds of USD 63.2 million including preliminary working capital adjustments, with a gain of USD 5.6 million over the nine months after USD 8.6 million in the second quarter and a USD 3.0 million loss in the third. The line had been added by the acquisition of Ozark Materials, completed on 2022-10-03 for USD 344.5 million and funded from existing credit facilities and cash; the sale was not treated as a discontinued operation.

Other transactions that matter to creditors are the settlement of the BASF litigation, agreed on 2026-03-13 after the appeal failed on 2026-02-11 and paid on 2026-04-01 at USD 113.2 million, and share repurchases of USD 126.3 million including excise tax in the nine months under a USD 500.0 million authorization of 2022-07-25. The strategic review of Advanced Polymer Technologies, announced on 2025-12-08, has produced no sale agreement in the filings, only the USD 32.1 million impairment recorded in the second quarter of 2026.

### T2D.9 Sponsor and governance risk assessment

Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by shareholder returns above free cash flow in 2026 and by portfolio and leadership change, because cash returned competes with debt repayment while the 2028 notes approach, which implies slower deleveraging and more refinancing risk. spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit for Ingevity Corp (issuer ngvt-1653477) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the integrated fundamental credit view of Ingevity Corporation, built from the five supplied filings and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses, with no rating, security, legal-capacity or portfolio conclusion.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_ngvt-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-02-19 (signature date) | d493022dfe6a796f38f9fb4d462a38c9e6081f53c7723bb5ab859f775ca642d3 | FY2023 and FY2024 context for earnings history and the Ozark Materials acquisition |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-26 (signature date) | 153c101c2e2c623a71bd5103a8766d49530b0a28e3a66ed6f6ced4cccb096ef2 | Business, customers, competition, risk factors, segment results for FY2023 to FY2025, income statement, capital expenditure, debt note, repurchases |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_ngvt-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-05-07 (signature date; filing date not stated) | 1dcc184b7bedeafb67aa8a87f8ab7b6127766dbd953589f0594b7f78ff5df0e3 | First-quarter events: revolver amendment, BASF settlement |

| Supplied analysis | Module | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness | CP-0 | d299f8a6fe463d0a3e8fa4a3a1cffa94e660b0f8b3fd06a54c89f1fc1f9f91ac | Source inventory and the open gaps on the proxy statement, financing agreements and covenant definitions |

| Financial foundation | CP-1 | b8476052ce85e783c7704bba51c78b7b2c644e672a8f4f9fc146af78429fc29b | Debt, net debt, last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, cash interest, liquidity, free cash flow and ratios at 2026-09-30; its post-balance-sheet table found no adjusting event |
| Business & governance | CP-1A | aa4d54aa3a3d0dd8581dd74c893961fd823ac00dd8cf2c65741dea1c076e51dd | Business mix, ownership, governance, transactions, capital allocation and behavior flags |
No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Ingevity's fundamental credit profile is adequate: one high-margin automotive carbon business supports moderate leverage and liquidity, but concentrated earnings, an unfinished portfolio reshaping and shareholder returns above free cash flow make the USD 550.0 million 2028 notes the pivot. Net debt is 2.75x LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 384.8 million, cash interest is covered 6.66x and liquidity is USD 398.2 million, yet Performance Materials segment EBITDA of USD 339.5 million equals 88.2% of that Adjusted EBITDA.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B1; calculation B2

The primary downside is weaker automotive volume in Asia and Europe while buybacks, which exceeded free cash flow in 2026, compete with debt repayment: an illustrative 20% fall in that segment's EBITDA would lift net debt to Adjusted EBITDA from 2.75x to 3.35x.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation B4
### Key findings

The strongest support is pricing power in a high-margin automotive carbon franchise. Performance Materials earned a margin of 53.8% in FY2025 and 55.6% in nine months of 2026, and price and mix added USD 14.3 million to nine-month sales against a USD 1.3 million volume loss, so earnings held while volumes stalled. Price now carries earnings, and the ten largest customers buy about 90% of sales in this business on purchase orders, so customer acceptance of price is the channel through which pressure would arrive.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B3

Earnings concentration is the weakest dimension. Performance Materials segment EBITDA of USD 339.5 million over the last twelve months is 88.2% of group Adjusted EBITDA of USD 384.8 million, while Pavement Technologies earned USD 44.4 million and Advanced Polymer Technologies USD 36.0 million, which after USD 35.1 million of corporate and indirect costs leave USD 45.3 million, or 11.8% of Adjusted EBITDA. Vehicle build, emissions rules and substitutes such as sealed fuel tanks and electric vehicles therefore act on almost all group cash flow.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; calculation B2; calculation B21

Leverage and interest cover are moderate on the issuer's measure but weak on an unadjusted one. Net debt is 2.75x and total debt 2.98x LTM Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 6.66x, and the issuer states covenant net leverage of 2.4x against a 4.0x maximum. FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 373.0 million carries add-backs of USD 336.8 million, 87.0% of them impairments, and net debt over unadjusted EBITDA is 5.35x for the last twelve months, so the adequate view depends on accepting the issuer's add-backs.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation B1; calculation B13

Liquidity is adequate for the next two years, but the committed backstop is smaller. Cash of USD 85.4 million and undrawn revolver capacity of USD 312.8 million give USD 398.2 million, which covers 5.21x the USD 76.4 million of near-term maturities not funded by a restricted trust, yet revolver commitments were cut from USD 1,000 million to USD 750 million on 2026-03-26. Capital expenditure gives some flexibility: USD 34.3 million for nine months and USD 50 million to USD 60 million guided for 2026 compare with depreciation and amortization of USD 65.6 million for nine months.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50; calculation B7; calculation B11; calculation B22

The 2028 notes are the pivotal refinancing. USD 550.0 million falls due on 2028-11-01, and if more than USD 250 million of the notes remain outstanding on 2028-08-02 the revolver, drawn at USD 425.0 million, matures early, so repayment or refinancing has to be settled before that date. Refinancing at the revolver's weighted rate of 5.20% would add about USD 7.26 million a year to interest as an illustration, and no rating or bond price is supplied to test market access.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 121; calculation B5; calculation B12

Free cash flow is real but volatile. Free cash flow was USD 51.0 million in FY2024, 14% of Adjusted EBITDA, USD 273.5 million in FY2025, 73%, and USD 49.1 million in nine months of 2026 after a USD 113.2 million litigation settlement and a USD 60.7 million outflow into trade working capital. The cash flow statements include the sold industrial specialties business, so conversion on the continuing perimeter is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; calculation B9; calculation B10

Financial policy is the main constraint. Cash repurchases of USD 125.3 million in nine months exceeded free cash flow of USD 49.1 million and USD 172.2 million of authorization remains, with no sponsor or controlling holder named to support the issuer or restrain returns. At the third-quarter pace of USD 38.9 million a quarter, suspending repurchases would conserve about USD 155.6 million a year, which is a lever fully within management's control.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation B16

Portfolio reshaping adds execution risk. Advanced Polymer Technologies earned USD 36.0 million of LTM segment EBITDA, so selling it lifts net debt to Adjusted EBITDA from 2.75x to 3.04x unless net proceeds of at least USD 99.2 million repay debt, and buyer feedback has already led to a USD 32.1 million impairment after a USD 183.8 million goodwill write-off in 2025. Acquisitions have not recovered their price on the evidence available: Ozark Materials cost USD 344.5 million and the road markings line sold for USD 63.2 million after a USD 109.3 million impairment, although the filings do not state that the two perimeters match.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-K_2024-12-31_ngvt-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 136; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation B6; calculation B23

The remaining pavement business is the weakest earner. Pavement Technologies earned a segment margin of 17.0% in nine months of 2026 against 18.5%, with USD 45.6 million of segment EBITDA against USD 61.5 million, and 70% to 75% of its revenue falls between April and September while higher asphalt costs soften customer demand. About USD 20 million of stranded costs from the two disposals are 65% removed, with 75% targeted by year end, and management guides Adjusted EBITDA of USD 385 million to USD 395 million for 2026.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; calculation B14
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that the balance sheet is already shrinking and the pivot can be handled early. Debt including finance leases fell USD 255.5 million from FY2024 to USD 1,145.5 million, revolver borrowings fell USD 270.0 million, liquidity is USD 398.2 million and the issuer reports covenant ratios of 2.4x and 7.0x. The cautious view would lose if the 2028 notes are refinanced or cut below USD 250 million before 2028-08-02, if sale proceeds above USD 99.2 million repay debt, and if buybacks slow from the USD 38.9 million quarterly pace.

The strongest evidence against treating concentration as the primary risk is stability: Performance Materials segment EBITDA rose 9.9% in FY2024 and fell only 2.1% in FY2025, while the other two segments fell 17.7% to 24.5% in single years, and management describes North American demand as resilient on hybrid vehicles. The concentration view would strengthen if volume declines widen beyond the 4% seen in the third quarter, if price and mix gains reverse or if a top customer is lost, since an illustrative 20% fall in Performance Materials EBITDA alone lifts net debt to Adjusted EBITDA to 3.35x.

### Strengths and weaknesses

The credit strengths, in rank order, are these. First, pricing power and margin in Performance Materials: a 55.6% nine-month margin and USD 14.3 million of price and mix against a USD 1.3 million volume loss mean earnings held while volume stalled, which supports debt service. Second, moderate leverage and cover: net debt is 2.75x LTM Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 6.66x, which leaves room to absorb a modest earnings decline. Third, adequate liquidity of USD 398.2 million with a revolver to 2031-03-31, which covers near-term maturities not funded by the trust 5.21x. Fourth, a record of debt reduction, USD 255.5 million since FY2024, which lowers the amount to refinance. Fifth, flexible capital expenditure and detailed, audited reporting, which allow cash preservation and lender monitoring.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B1; calculation B7; calculation B15

The credit weaknesses, in rank order, are these. First, earnings concentration: Performance Materials segment EBITDA is 88.2% of Adjusted EBITDA, so one end market sets group cash flow. Second, the USD 550.0 million 2028 notes and the springing revolver maturity, which force a refinancing decision before 2028-08-02. Third, shareholder returns above free cash flow, with USD 125.3 million of cash repurchases against USD 49.1 million of free cash flow and no sponsor or controlling holder to restrain or support. Fourth, an unfinished portfolio reshaping with large write-downs of acquired assets, where a sale of Advanced Polymer Technologies raises leverage unless net proceeds reach USD 99.2 million. Fifth, earnings quality, because FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA includes add-backs of USD 336.8 million.

### Company description

Ingevity is a specialty chemicals and materials group with three reportable segments: Performance Materials, which sells hardwood-based activated carbon for gasoline vapor control in combustion and hybrid vehicles and for filtration, was 52.0% of FY2025 net sales; Pavement Technologies, named Performance Chemicals until the second quarter of 2026, sells asphalt additives, emulsifiers and agrochemical dispersants and was 34.3% including road markings; and Advanced Polymer Technologies, which sells caprolactone polymers, was 13.7%. Sales go to about 65 automotive customers, about 600 pavement customers and about 200 polymer customers, 43% of FY2025 sales were outside the United States, and the group sold the industrial specialties business on 2026-01-01 and road markings on 2026-04-15.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation B18; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Cash-flow visibility is moderate: sales to the largest customers rest mainly on purchase orders, pavement revenue is seasonal and government-funded, and the company is smaller and simpler than a year ago, so debt service depends on pricing power in carbon holding while the portfolio settles. Customer stickiness is higher in automotive carbon, where the annual report cites a decades-long record of meeting life-of-vehicle emission standards, a company characterization, than in pavement, where competitors are named and demand follows paving budgets.
### Ownership and group structure

Ingevity is a widely held New York Stock Exchange company with just over four thousand holders of record and no sponsor, parent or controlling holder named in the filings; the only outside investor named, Vision One Fund, settled a board contest by cooperation agreement on 2025-03-30 and its stake is not stated. The 2025 annual report takes board, ownership and related-party information from a proxy statement that is not supplied, so ownership, independence and insider holdings are not established.

The revolving credit agreement names Ingevity Corporation, Ingevity Holdings SRL and Ingevity UK Ltd as parties, with Ingevity UK added as a borrower in 2022, the 2028 notes carry unnamed subsidiary guarantors, and receivables are financed through a wholly owned special purpose entity, so structural seniority and the guarantor perimeter cannot be drawn from the filings. Financial policy is shareholder-return led: no cash dividend appears, cash repurchases were USD 125.3 million in nine months of 2026, and no owner exists to inject equity, so support in stress would have to come from asset sales or liquidity, not from a holder.

### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is cyclical, concentrated and price-led. Performance Materials sales follow gasoline and hybrid vehicle production, with about half of sales in North America and about 40% in Asia Pacific, and in the third quarter volume fell USD 6.7 million, or four percent, on softness in China and Europe while price and mix added USD 5.4 million. Because the ten largest customers take about 90% of sales and buy on purchase orders, a price concession or a lost customer would move earnings quickly, and the annual report names sealed fuel tanks and electric vehicles as substitutes that would cut demand over time.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation B3

Pavement Technologies depends on government infrastructure spending through about 600 customers, earns 70% to 75% of revenue between April and September and reported that higher asphalt costs limited sales growth, so its sales excluding road markings rose only 1% in the third quarter. Advanced Polymer Technologies raised sales USD 14.9 million in nine months mainly through price and mix of USD 9.9 million including surcharges, which recovered input costs with little margin gain, and it faces new entrants and competing materials.
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins can be defended in Performance Materials but are squeezed elsewhere. Group gross margin was 44.3% in nine months of 2026 against 40.9%, a rise of 3.3 percentage points that the quarterly report attributes to price and mix of USD 29.3 million, partly offset by volume and manufacturing costs. Manufacturing costs rose USD 8.6 million in Pavement Technologies and USD 8.0 million in Advanced Polymer Technologies, so those segments cannot yet pass costs through at a gain, whereas Performance Materials cut manufacturing cost by USD 8.3 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 42–44; calculation B8

The cost base is energy- and raw-material-intensive: natural gas powers carbon and chemical plants and is partly hedged, lignin and tall oil fatty acid are in limited supply, hydrogen peroxide comes from one named supplier, and several products are made at one plant, so operating leverage is high if volume falls. Management expects about USD 20 million of stranded costs from the two disposals to fall by 75% by the end of 2026, with 65% already removed on an annualised basis, which would support the guided margins if delivered.
### Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion

Capital intensity is moderate and flexible. Capital expenditure was 4.94% of FY2025 net sales, maintenance spending was USD 34.8 million in FY2025 and USD 22.1 million in nine months of 2026, and 2026 guidance of USD 50 million to USD 60 million sits below nine-month depreciation and amortization of USD 65.6 million, so spending can be cut to preserve cash. Conversion of Adjusted EBITDA to free cash flow was 14% in FY2024, 73% in FY2025 and 32% over the last twelve months, because restructuring cash, litigation and working capital swing the result.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 67–68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 50–51; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B10; calculation B11

Nine-month 2026 free cash flow of USD 49.1 million was after a USD 113.2 million settlement and a USD 60.7 million outflow into trade working capital against USD 3.8 million a year earlier, while receivables financing rose USD 31.1 million; cash taxes of USD 2.4 million are low against a guided effective tax rate of 22% to 24%. Cash interest was USD 38.1 million in nine months, USD 12.6 million lower than a year earlier, and 100 bp on the USD 500.0 million of variable-rate borrowings adds about USD 5.0 million a year.

### Porter's five forces

Rivalry is moderate where the company has differentiation and higher where it has not. In activated carbon the annual report names Norit, Kuraray, domestic producers and Chinese manufacturers, in pavement Nouryon, Arkema and Zydex, and in caprolactone Daicel, Hunan Juren and BASF, so Performance Materials margin of 55.6% implies protection that the other two segments, at 17.0% and 22.0%, do not show. Rivalry therefore threatens margin mainly in the segments that earn 11.8% of group Adjusted EBITDA after corporate costs.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; calculation B2; calculation B3

The threat of new entrants is low in automotive carbon on the company's account of decades of meeting life-of-vehicle standards, but real in caprolactone, where new market entrants are cited, and Chinese manufacturers compete in carbon. The threat of substitutes is the largest long-term force: sealed fuel tanks reduce honeycomb use and electric and hydrogen vehicles reduce carbon demand, and competing monomers, thermoplastics and polyols challenge caprolactone, so substitution would hit the 88.2% earnings concentration directly.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation B2

Buyer power is high in automotive carbon, with about 65 customers, ten taking about 90% of sales and purchase-order terms, and low in pavement, with about 600 customers and the ten largest at about 38% of the line. Supplier power is moderate: sawdust and phosphoric acid have multiple suppliers, while lignin and tall oil fatty acid are in limited supply and hydrogen peroxide comes from one named supplier, which could disrupt pavement and polymer output if supply fails.
### PEST factors

Regulatory and political factors are material. Emission standards set carbon demand and the annual report names the risk that standards are not tightened, retaliatory tariffs by China could lower margin on carbon and chemicals exported from the United States, and pavement demand follows government infrastructure budgets. Economic factors are also material: crude-oil-driven asphalt costs limited pavement growth, 43% of FY2025 sales were outside the United States with exposure to the euro, yen, pound, real and renminbi, and a hypothetical 10 percent adverse move in three currencies would cut nine-month net sales by USD 11.1 million. Technological change is the most important: electric and hydrogen vehicles and sealed tanks threaten automotive carbon demand over time, and social factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver.
### SWOT

Strengths are a high-margin carbon franchise with pricing power, moderate leverage of 2.75x, liquidity of USD 398.2 million and a revolver to 2031-03-31, and a record of reducing debt by USD 255.5 million. Weaknesses are earnings concentration at 88.2%, shareholder returns above free cash flow, a low-margin and seasonal pavement business, and earnings quality that depends on add-backs of USD 336.8 million in FY2025.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; calculation B1; calculation B2; calculation B13; calculation B15

Opportunities that could improve credit quality are an Advanced Polymer Technologies sale with net proceeds above USD 99.2 million applied to debt, a refinancing of the 2028 notes ahead of 2028-08-02, delivery of the 75% stranded cost reduction, and growth in filtration and energy storage uses of carbon that the company says it is exploring. Threats are faster substitution away from combustion and hybrid vehicles, tariff escalation, a failed or delayed sale, further buybacks funded from sale proceeds, and asphalt cost inflation reducing pavement demand.
Basis: calculation B6; calculation B12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 25–27
### Financial profile and credit quality

On a ratings-style lens, scale and market position are average: net sales of USD 1,132.3 million over the last twelve months are mid-sized and the company names a long carbon track record, but the portfolio is shrinking. Competitive advantage is strong in Performance Materials, on a margin of 53.8% in FY2025, and average elsewhere; business diversification is weak, because one segment earns 88.2% of Adjusted EBITDA; cost and capex flexibility is average, with capital expenditure guided below depreciation but single-site plants and energy exposure; and margin stability is average, with Performance Materials steady between 53.8% and 55.6% and pavement margins falling.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; calculation B2; calculation B3; calculation B11

Free cash flow stability is average, since conversion swung between 14% and 73% on restructuring, litigation and working capital; the ability to refinance is average, resting on a USD 550.0 million 2028 maturity with a springing revolver test and no observable market price; and liquidity is average, at USD 398.2 million against a revolver cut to USD 750 million. Financial policy and governance is average: reporting is detailed and audited and covenant ratios are stated, but repurchases of USD 125.3 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 49.1 million, leadership and the board changed in 2024 and 2025, and no owner supports or restrains the issuer. The trend is improving on debt and margin and uncertain on policy, and the key missing datapoints are the financing agreements, the proxy statement and the funding of repurchases.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

In the next 12 to 24 months management guides net sales of about USD 1.1 billion and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 385 million to USD 395 million for 2026, with Performance Materials margins in the mid-50s percent, pavement in the mid-teens and Advanced Polymer Technologies near 20%, which implies fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 70.5 million to USD 80.5 million. Tailwinds are price and mix gains, the stranded cost removal, lower cash interest and the January 2027 finance lease being funded from a restricted trust; headwinds are weaker automotive volume in China and Europe, asphalt costs, tariffs and a possible Advanced Polymer Technologies sale that removes earnings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 42–43; calculation B14; calculation B19

Over three to five years the 2028 notes and the springing revolver test fall inside the horizon, and the structural headwind is the transition from combustion and hybrid vehicles, which the company aims to offset by growing products for electric and hydrogen vehicles. Company-specific tailwinds are a smaller portfolio and lower leverage, while sector headwinds are substitution and infrastructure funding risk, so the medium-term outlook depends on whether proceeds and cash flow reduce debt before the 2028 test date.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation B12
### Downside scenario

The downside path starts with weaker gasoline and hybrid vehicle build in China and Europe, already visible as a USD 6.7 million third-quarter volume loss, combined with tariff retaliation that can lower margin on carbon exported from the United States to China. The first operational break is lower carbon volume that price and mix can no longer offset, because buyers on purchase orders can resist increases; an illustrative 20% fall in Performance Materials EBITDA removes USD 67.9 million from a base of USD 339.5 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation B4

The financial transmission is Adjusted EBITDA of USD 316.9 million, net debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 3.35x on unchanged net debt and cash interest cover of 5.48x, with last-twelve-month free cash flow of about USD 54.7 million before any tax effect against USD 125.3 million of repurchases in nine months. Liquidity of USD 398.2 million still covers near-term maturities 5.21x, so a liquidity crisis is not implied, but the stress lands on the 2028 refinancing: leverage near 3.35x with an unfinished sale and no rating or market price makes refinancing the USD 550.0 million notes by 2028-08-02 harder.
Basis: calculation B4; calculation B7; calculation B12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5

Management has levers: suspending repurchases would conserve about USD 155.6 million a year at the third-quarter pace, capital expenditure can fall toward maintenance of USD 34.8 million, and an Advanced Polymer Technologies sale above USD 99.2 million applied to debt offsets lost earnings. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in this scenario if the levers are used, and the observable triggers are a fall in Performance Materials volumes beyond four percent, a quarterly Adjusted EBITDA run rate below the guided range, repurchases continuing while free cash flow is below them, and no refinancing plan for the 2028 notes by the 2027 annual report.
Basis: calculation B16; 10-K_2025-12-31_ngvt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 67–68; calculation B6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ngvt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47
### Overall credit view

Overall, Ingevity presents an adequate business profile supported by a high-margin automotive carbon franchise with pricing power, moderate leverage of 2.75x and liquidity of USD 398.2 million, but credit quality is constrained by earnings concentration, shareholder returns above free cash flow and an unfinished portfolio reshaping. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because price and mix, a flexible capital expenditure budget and a shrinking debt balance offset volume softness, although free cash flow swung between 14% and 73% of Adjusted EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on whether an Advanced Polymer Technologies sale repays debt, on the pace of repurchases, and on handling the USD 550.0 million 2028 notes before the revolver test on 2028-08-02. Primary downside path: weaker automotive volume in Asia and Europe lowering Performance Materials EBITDA, which carries 88.2% of Adjusted EBITDA, while repurchases and an unfinished sale leave leverage higher into the 2028 refinancing. Further analysis would require the financing agreements, the proxy statement, the use of disposal proceeds, a rating or bond price and any sale agreement for Advanced Polymer Technologies. Top risk: concentration of earnings in automotive carbon combined with the 2028 refinancing.
